_why: Capability OBSERVATIONS about the three harnesses, each pinned to the version it was measured on. Codex and Antigravity ship almost daily, so a sentence like 'this flag does not exist' is evidence about one build, never a ruling. npm run harness:usage compares measuredOn with the installed version and prints every observation that is now UNVERIFIED, with the probe that re-settles it. A CONSTRAINT is different: it comes from our own rules or a contract we own, does not lapse with a release, and is listed here only so a reader can tell the two apart. Append; never delete - a lapsed observation gets re-measured and its measuredOn moves.

observations.claim: REFUTED as of 1.1.27: the same reprobe call (npm run agy:read, no command grant, "list the files in <dir>") returned a complete, accurate directory listing instead of an empty response. Whatever changed - a new real grant path for a listing action, or something else - the empty-response behavior described below is gone; this was not re-derived further. Previously measured true on 1.1.25 (2026-09-03): headless agy auto-denies any tool with no grant and still returns status SUCCESS with an empty response; only read_file, command and write_file were real grant actions (list_dir, grep_search, codebase_search were accepted into settings.json and dropped as invalid).
observations.reprobe: npm run agy:read -- --model gemini-3.7-flash-high --label reprobe-grants "List the files in <an absolute worktree dir>" with no command grant; an empty response confirms the original claim, a listing confirms the refutation.
observations.source: docs/HARNESS_ROUTING.md, "Three facts about this machine that were not true when this file last said them"; refuted by the 2026-09-09 capability re-probe, commit 1a51192f

observations.claim: claude-sonnet-4-6 and claude-opus-4-6-thinking reject --effort outright (status ERROR, 0 s, 0 tokens); the Gemini and GPT-OSS ids carry their tier in the model name.

observations.claim: agy keeps no cumulative usage on disk and has no usage or quota subcommand; per-run usage exists once on stdout, which is why scripts/agy-run.mjs is the only record of Antigravity spend.
observations.reprobe: agy --help for a usage/quota subcommand, and a text scan of ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ for a token field after one run.
observations.source: scripts/agy-run.mjs header; docs/HARNESS_ROUTING.md "Cost, and what a usage meter can read"

observations.claim: codex agents is a TUI with no --json or list-and-exit mode, so Codex jobs cannot join the third liveness signal the way claude agents --json does; codex queue is fire-and-forget into a thread you already hold.

observations.claim: Codex writes a rate_limits snapshot into its rollout only when one of its own sessions runs, so the capacity reading can be absent or stale; availability is three-valued (headroom / low / UNKNOWN) and is never probed with a paid call.
observations.reprobe: npm run harness:usage after a Codex session; the snapshot line names its own timestamp.
observations.source: docs/HARNESS_ROUTING.md, "Owner ruling 2026-09-01: route by pool capacity"

observations.claim: An Agent call with isolation: "remote" is ACCEPTED and runs on this laptop anyway, in an ordinary local worktree (hostname Legion-001, win32, .claude/worktrees/agent-<id>). The launch reports success and nothing says the isolation was dropped, so a wave routing rows to "cloud" spends the local RAM it meant to save while the plan still reads as honoured.
observations.reprobe: Launch any agent with isolation: "remote" whose first step is `node scripts/agent-isolation.mjs --expect remote`. Exit 1 with ISOLATION MISMATCH confirms it; exit 0 refutes it and this entry moves.

observations.claim: PARTLY REFUTED, then CORRECTED the same day on 2.1.263. The routing is neither 'always the launcher' nor 'always the session': a subagent's completion notification goes to WHOEVER IS INSIDE A TURN when it fires. Measured both ways. (a) Two probes had a launched session spawn a subagent and stay inside a turn - one explicitly sat in a 120-second blocking command - and the notification arrived in that session, carrying the subagent's final message verbatim. (b) A controlled probe had a launched session spawn one background subagent and END ITS TURN immediately; that notification arrived in the LAUNCHER, and the marker file confirmed the subagent had run, so 'no notification' is not confounded with 'never ran'. (c) In the field, sixteen fan-out reports have strayed to a launcher: seven from one row on 2026-09-08 and eight from another on 2026-09-09. A FAN-OUT IS ALWAYS CASE (b), because a session that has spawned agents has nothing left to do but end its turn and wait - which is why waiting on one never works and why the original observation held in practice for the case that matters. The earlier note here, that this was simply 'REFUTED', was measured correctly and generalised wrongly from the stay-in-turn case alone. Consequence for a launcher: stray reports belong to the row that spawned them - relay them with scripts/relay.mjs rather than acting on them. Previously measured true on 2.1.240 (2026-09-03): a session launched by another session never receives its own subagents' completion notifications; they route to the launcher.
observations.reprobe: Two probes, and they must be run as a PAIR or the answer is half true. From a launched session: (1) spawn a background subagent and stay inside one long blocking call - the notification should arrive in that session at the turn boundary; (2) spawn one and end the turn immediately - it should arrive in the launcher. Confirm the subagent actually ran via a marker file in both cases.
observations.source: .agent-workflows/orchestrator/incidents.md, "the fan-out that waited on notifications that could not arrive"; refuted by the 2026-09-09 capability re-probe, commit 1a51192f

observations.claim: PARTIALLY REFUTED as of 2.1.263: `claude agents --json` still answers in under a second with pid and cwd, but the objects no longer carry a status field at all (kind, startedAt and sessionId appear instead) - anything reading `status` off this command now reads undefined rather than a stale or wrong value. Previously measured true on 2.1.251 (2026-09-03): claude agents --json answered in under a second with pid, cwd and status, and was the third liveness signal beside the two transcript-based ones.
observations.reprobe: node scripts/claude-agents.mjs; it probes the command's shape on every run and degrades to unknown by itself. A `status` in the raw `claude agents --json` output confirms the original claim; its absence confirms the refutation.
observations.source: .agent-workflows/orchestrator/incidents.md, "the third liveness signal"; refuted by the 2026-09-09 capability re-probe, commit 1a51192f

observations.claim: scripts/agy-run.mjs refuses --dangerously-skip-permissions rather than forwarding it, and a write runs only in a linked worktree on a feature branch. This is our rule, not a fact about agy, and it does not lapse with a release.

A Codex row always names a fallback pool, because Codex capacity is shared with the owner's other projects and can be near zero on a given day. Codex is otherwise available by default (owner, 2026-09-03) - this constrains the plan's shape, not how much Codex it uses.

A delegation's writable root is THE LAUNCHING SESSION'S WORKING DIRECTORY, and nothing else. Measured three times on 2026-09-09, and the third attempt CONFIRMS the rule by succeeding. First, handed the ordinary row recipe ('make a feature branch in its own worktree before the work starts'), the delegate was denied writing C:/claude/NoaCG-Studio/.git/refs/heads/<branch> and stopped having changed no file. Then, given a worktree created for it in advance and told to run no git at all, it refused again and said why in plain terms: the target 'is outside that writable root, and approval is disabled', naming the launching session's own worktree as the only writable path. It read both target files correctly and reported its analysis, so reads are unrestricted; only writes are pinned. CONSEQUENCE FOR ROUTING: pre-creating a worktree does NOT help, because the root follows the launcher, not the prompt. A delegation can only edit files under the directory the launching session is sitting in. Either launch it from a session whose cwd IS the worktree the work belongs in, or have it edit in the launcher's own checkout and move the result. Third attempt, launched from a session whose OWN working directory was the target worktree: it created a new module and edited three existing files there without complaint. So the rule is positive as well as negative - delegate from the session that sits where the result belongs and it simply works. This is the mechanical reason such delegations get recorded as attempted and never landed, and it is not fixed by choosing the harness more often.
observations.reprobe: Delegate a one-line edit to a file in a DIFFERENT worktree from the launching session's, and read whether it reports the path as outside its writable root. The refusal names the root, which is the answer.
observations.source: docs/HARNESS_ROUTING.md - the delegate that cannot make its own branch
